title: Add NVTX ranges, per-core counters, microbench harness and perf dashboard for runtime profiling
author: Ava Chen
description:
Motivation: We need stronger end-to-end profiling signals in the runtime to diagnose perf regressions (kernel selection, scheduling hotspots, KV cache effectiveness, batching tail latency). This PR adds NVTX ranges around key runtime stages, lightweight atomic counters for KV-cache and scheduler events, a small microbenchmark harness to exercise common code paths, and a Grafana/JSON dashboard + docs to make the signals consumable by SRE and eng teams.

What this PR includes: checklist: [x] NVTX range annotations in runtime executor (enqueue, schedule, kernel_launch, kv_cache_lookup, kv_cache_insert, batch_build) [x] Atomic counters exposed via metrics endpoint (kv_cache_hits, kv_cache_misses, kv_read_bytes, kv_write_bytes, scheduler_queue_depth, batch_sizes_histogram) [x] Microbench harness (tools/microbench/nvtx_bench) to run kernel and batching hot loops with NVTX markers and output structured CSV for later correlation with perf runs [x] Grafana dashboard jsonnet in observability/dashboards/runtime_profiling.jsonnet with prebuilt panels (NVTX range durations mapped to timeline, counters over time, microbench summary) [x] Documentation page with how-to (docs/perf/instrumentation.md) and runbook for investigating regressions.

Testing: unit tests added for counter correctness and a small integration smoke test that validates NVTX calls don't crash when NVTX absent on the system (runtime uses weak linkage). Microbench runs were executed on p4d and g5 instances; sample numbers attached below. CI: all builds passed (unit, integration, lint), coverage unchanged.

Performance summary: microbench (p4d, 2048 tokens, batch=8) shows wall-time breakdown: batching 12.3ms, kernel_launch 54.1ms, kv_cache_lookup 1.2ms (cache-hit scenario) compared to previous uninstrumented baseline - instrumentation overhead measured <1.5% in hot path when NVTX disabled at runtime.

Rollout plan: merged to main, will enable dashboard via observability pipeline and flip sampling flags in staging for 2 weeks before enabling in production dashboards.

Notes: NVTX calls are guarded by a runtime flag and weak-linked to avoid runtime dependency; counters use std::atomic and integrate with existing metrics exporter. See linked Linear tasks for follow-ups: ENG-2314 (add structured KV cache event sampling) and ENG-2480 (scheduler trace sampling).

review_comments: Mateo Rivera: Please gate NVTX calls with the runtime flag and ensure weak linking for systems without NVTX; also add a CI smoke test that runs when NVTX lib is not present.
Ava Chen (author): Addressed - NVTX invocation wrapped in RuntimeTrace::ScopedRange and weak-linked; added instrumentation_smoke_test that stubs missing nvtx symbols.
Priya Patel: Counters look good. Can you avoid global atomics and prefer per-thread sharded counters aggregated on scrape? Concern about contention at very high QPS.

Ava Chen (author): Added sharded counters for high-cardinality paths (scheduler queue depth uses sharded buckets) and left KV counters as atomics because KV cache paths are already per-worker and contention was negligible in microbench.
Daniel Kim: Dashboard panels are useful. Can we add a panel that correlates NVTX range durations with batch size to spot tail latency causes?
Ava Chen (author): Added batch-size correlation panel and included CSV output mapping microbench batch sizes to NVTX timing buckets for offline analysis.
Priya Patel: Approved after responses and a green CI run.
Mateo Rivera: LGTM. Merging with squash.
release_notes: Added runtime instrumentation: NVTX ranges, microbench harness, counters and perf dashboard for easier profiling and regression analysis. No customer-facing API changes.
additional_context: Follow-ups: ENG-2314 (structured KV-cache sampling), ENG-2480 (scheduler trace sampling rollout), ENG-2567 (add eBPF overlay for kernel-level tracing)
This PR intentionally keeps NVTX as optional to avoid adding a hard dependency on systems that don't have NVIDIA tooling available.
